Abuse","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":462,"printedEnd":469,"pdfStart":480,"pdfEnd":487,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Substance use can engage reward pathways and change motivation over time. The text examines dopamine, cravings, tolerance, withdrawal, and attempts to reduce stress through drug use."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Genetic and behavioral predispositions affect risk, and treatments differ across substances. Distinguish short-term drug effects from adaptations that contribute to repeated use, and distinguish treatments for alcohol and opioid-related problems."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-1-study-1","text":"Substance use and reinforcement"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Psychoactive substances influence brain signaling in different ways, and repeated use can alter motivation and behavior. The reward-related role of dopamine is important but should not be translated into the simplistic claim that dopamine means pleasure or directly causes all addictions. Learning, expectation, environment, and stress influence the likelihood of seeking a substance. A substance-use problem involves persistent harmful patterns, not just the presence of a chemical in the body."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-1-study-2","text":"Tolerance, withdrawal, and craving"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Tolerance describes a reduced response to a repeated dose or a need for more of a substance to produce a previous effect. Withdrawal refers to reactions that may occur when use is reduced or stopped after adaptation. Craving is a strong motivation or urge to use. These processes can occur together but are not interchangeable, and not all drugs produce identical patterns. Learned cues can trigger seeking even after acute withdrawal has passed, showing that addiction involves more than physical dependence."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-1-study-3","text":"Why risk differs"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Genetic predispositions, environmental exposure, stress, learning history, and the specific pharmacological actions of a drug all contribute to risk. Studies of alcohol and opioid-related problems illustrate both shared and distinct mechanisms. A person's course cannot be predicted from one dopamine measurement or one family-history fact. Distinguish susceptibility from inevitability, and examine why certain settings increase the probability that drug use is repeated."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-1-study-4","text":"Treatment principles"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Different treatments aim to reduce harmful use, manage withdrawal, block or substitute some drug effects, and change learned behavioral patterns. Medication and behavioral strategies can complement one another, depending on the substance and circumstances. Successful recovery often requires addressing social and environmental conditions as well as neural adaptation. Because drug problems have multiple influences, no one intervention is appropriate for every person."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h01","text":"Drug Effects"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Nicotine comes from tobacco, caffeine from coffee and tea, opiates from poppies, and cocaine from coca.","sourcePrintedPage":462,"sourcePdfPage":480,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A drug that blocks a neurotransmitter is an antagonist , whereas a drug that mimics or increases the effects is an agonist . (The term agonist is derived from a Greek word meaning “contestant.” The term agony derives from the same root.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An antagonist is an “anti-agonist,” or member of the opposing team.) A mixed agonist–antagonist is an agonist for some effects and an antagonist for others, or an agonist at some doses and an antagonist at others.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Investigators say that a drug has an affinity for a receptor if it binds to it, like a key into a lock.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The effectiveness and side effects of any drug vary from one person to another, because drugs affect several kinds of receptors.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One person might have more dopamine type D 4 receptors and fewer D 1 or D 2 receptors, whereas someone else has the reverse .","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h02","text":"The Role of Dopamine"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"James Olds and Peter Milner wanted to test whether stimulation of a certain brain area might influence which direction a rat turns.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To their surprise, when the rat received the brain stimulation, it sat up, looked around, and sniffed, as if reacting to a favorable stimulus.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Stimulant drugs such as cocaine and amphetamine increase or prolong the release of dopamine in the nucleus accumbens .","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Nicotine stimulates neurons that release dopamine , and opiates inhibit neurons that inhibit dopamine release.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"dopamine in the nucleus accumbens , along with music , the taste of sugar , and simply imagining something pleasant .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although it seems natural to assume from all this that dopamine mediates pleasure, much research makes that idea seem uncertain .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Dopamine is important for the motivation to get something (wanting), but not necessarily for enjoying it.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with decreased dopamine, such as Parkinson’s disease patients, can still enjoy a tasty treat, apparently as much as ever.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h03","text":"Cravings"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Seeing a lit cigarette triggers a craving in smokers , a video of cocaine use triggers cravings in cocaine users , and the sight of a videogame triggers craving in an excessive videogame player .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most people who become addicted to a substance do not enjoy the experience as much as before, but they continue to want it .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cravings are persistent because of changes in the brain.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As Nora Volkow and others have demonstrated, after people become addicted to a drug, the drug releases less dopamine, but cues associated with the drug release more .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cues for the drug attract even more attention because of the decreased competition .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"These results match indications that craving increases during the early stage of abstinence, and slightly declines later .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Repeated alcohol or cocaine use also decreases blood flow and metabolism in the prefrontal cortex, resulting in decreased ability to restrain impulses .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h04","text":"Tolerance and Withdrawal"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because of tolerance, heroin users raise their amount and frequency of use to greater and greater levels, eventually taking amounts that could kill other people.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, rats that consistently receive a drug in a distinctive location show more tolerance there than elsewhere .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cues associated with receiving the drug activate learned mechanisms that counteract the effects of the drug.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because tolerance is learned, it can be weakened through extinction procedures.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If the rat then receives repeated injections of salt water without morphine, it weakens its learned connection between injection and morphine.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The result is decreased tolerance the next time it receives a morphine injection .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As the body comes to expect the drug, it reacts strongly when the drug is absent.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The withdrawal symptoms after someone quits heroin or other opiates include anxiety, sweating, vomiting, and diarrhea.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Efforts to avoid withdrawal symptoms contribute to addictive behaviors, but they are generally a minor contributor.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h05","text":"Drug Use for Stress Reduction"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One reason for an addiction is that a user learns to use the substance (or gambling habit or other addiction) to cope with stress.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers gave rats an opportunity to press a lever to inject themselves with heroin.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Midway through the withdrawal period, some of the rats had an opportunity to self-administer heroin again, while others went through withdrawal without heroin.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Later, when rats went through withdrawal a second time, all the rats had an opportunity to press a lever to try to get heroin, but this time, the lever was inoperative.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Evidently, receiving an addictive drug during a withdrawal period is a powerful experience.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h06","text":"Predispositions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most people drink alcohol in moderation, but others develop a habit of abuse.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even among mice, some develop compulsive alcohol use when given the opportunity, and some do not .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A great deal of the predisposition depends on experience.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People who had abusive experiences in childhood are more vulnerable, as is a child whose mother drank too much alcohol during pregnancy .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Children who grew up without careful parental supervision are more likely to develop impulse problems than children of more attentive parents .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As a rule, people with early-onset alcoholism (before age 25) have a family history of alcoholism, a genetic predisposition, and a rapid onset of the problem.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h07","text":"Genetic Influences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The probability of abusing alcohol or other drugs also relates to genetic influences.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Parents’ alcohol use correlates more strongly with that of their biological children than their adopted children .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Several genes affect the probability of substance use, with effects that vary from one environment to another .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most of these genes are non-specific, increasing the risk of several mental disorders, and risk-taking behaviors in general .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One gene with a well-confirmed influence on alcohol abuse controls the metabolism of alcohol.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In fact, this is the only case of a common gene with a substantial effect on a human psychological disorder (other than Huntington’s disease).","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with a gene that produces less acetaldehyde dehydrogenase metabolize acetaldehyde more slowly.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If they drink much alcohol, they accumulate acetaldehyde, which produces flushing of the face, increased heart rate, nausea, headache, abdominal pain, impaired breathing, and tissue damage.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h08","text":"Behavioral Predictors of Abuse"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If genes, early environment, or anything else predisposes certain people to drug or alcohol abuse, presumably the predisposition alters behavioral reactions to the substance.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"By the time someone has developed a serious substance abuse problem, overcoming it is difficult.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Such studies find that alcoholism is more likely among those who were described in childhood as impulsive, risk taking, easily bored, sensation seeking, and outgoing .","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because of the strong familial tendency toward alcoholism, researchers expect that many of the sons of alcoholics are future alcoholics themselves.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The most robust finding is that most sons of alcoholics show less than average intoxication after drinking a moderate amount of alcohol.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Presumably, someone who starts feeling tipsy after a couple of drinks stops at that point.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Follow-up studies found that men who report low intoxication after moderate drinking are more likely than others to develop an alcohol abuse problem .","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h09","text":"Treatments"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research has revealed much about the mechanisms of addiction.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Unfortunately, our increased understanding has not yet translated into better forms of treatment .","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In fact, that is the case for psychopathology in general.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research over recent decades has learned much about the genes, neurotransmitters, and other biological","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"factors related to disorders, but treatment outcomes have not improved noticeably .","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The most common treatment for substance abuse, especially in the United States, is participation in Alcoholics Anonymous, Narcotics Anonymous, or similar organizations.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A smaller number of people consult a psychotherapist.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Not many people turn to medications, but a few options are available.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h10","text":"Medications to Combat Alcohol Abuse"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As mentioned, the liver metabolizes alcohol into acetaldehyde (toxic) and then into acetic acid (harmless).","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The drug disulfiram, which goes by the trade name Antabuse , antagonizes the enzyme that metabolizes acetaldehyde.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Ordinarily, that result would indicate that a drug is ineffective, but Antabuse is a special case because of why it is similar to the placebo.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Antabuse is about equal to placebo not because Antabuse is ineffective, but because thinking that a placebo might be Antabuse makes the placebo effective .","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A related idea is to have people drink alcohol and then immediately take a drug that produces nausea, thereby forming a learned aversion to the taste of the alcohol.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That procedure usually produces quick and effective avoidance of alcohol, although its use has never been popular .","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Other medications are naloxone (trade name Revia) and naltrexone, which block opiate receptors and thereby decrease the pleasure from alcohol.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h11","text":"Medications to Combat Opiate Abuse"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some physicians at the time recommended that people using alcohol switch to heroin .","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Still, the idea has persisted that people who cannot quit opiates might switch to a less harmful drug.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Methadone (METH-uh-don), similar to heroin and morphine, activates the same brain receptors and produces the same effects, but it has the advantage that it can be taken orally.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Methadone taken orally slowly enters the blood and then the brain, avoiding a “rush” that disrupts behavior.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because methadone leaves the brain slowly, the withdrawal symptoms are also gradual.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Buprenorphine and levomethadyl acetate (LAAM), drugs similar to methadone, are also used to treat opiate addiction.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Anecdotal reports have stated that a drug called ibogaine reduces cravings and decreases the probability of drug relapse.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, ibogaine causes hallucinations, and it can damage the heart.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"So far, we know that it reduces alcohol and heroin seeking in mice, and we await results from human trials .","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h12","text":"In Closing: The Psychology and Biology of Substance Abuse"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many people say that alcoholism or other drug addiction is a disease.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Dis-ease is literally lack of ease, so in a sense anything that causes difficulty in life is a disease.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, the term disease is generally taken to imply that the problem calls for medical intervention.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Addiction alters the brain’s reaction to the drug, cues for the drug, and other events.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Addiction is a complex problem that requires attention to both the physiology and the social environment.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They’re also presented in alphabetical order with definitions in the book’s Subject Index/Glossary at the end of this book.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The research on sensitization of the nucleus accumbens dealt with addictive drugs, mainly cocaine.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Nearly all neurotransmitters and hormones are the same in humans as in other species.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":462,"sourcePdfPage":480},{"type":"bullet","text":"So, if a plant evolves a chemical to attract bees, repel caterpillars, or whatever, that chemical is likely to affect humans also.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":462,"sourcePdfPage":480},{"type":"bullet","text":"A drug’s efficacy is its tendency to activate the receptor.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481},{"type":"bullet","text":"A drug that binds to a receptor but fails to stimulate it has affinity but not efficacy.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481},{"type":"bullet","text":"When a pair of young psychologists were trying to answer an unrelated question, their accidental findings led to the discovery of the importance of dopamine in motivation.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481},{"type":"bullet","text":"When they implanted their electrode, they missed the intended target and instead hit an area called the septum.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481},{"type":"bullet","text":"Gambling activates this area for habitual gamblers, and videogame playing activates it for habitual videogame players.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"You might like a fattening dessert without wanting it, and you might want a medicine without liking it.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"Even after prolonged abstinence, cues associated with the habit trigger a renewed craving.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"Even after a long period of abstinence, the cues continue to grab attention and trigger a craving.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"During a period of abstinence, the nucleus accumbens synapses responding to drug cues become even more sensitive for a while, before partly declining later.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"After many injections of morphine, a rat develops tolerance to it.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"Symptoms of alcohol withdrawal include irritability, fatigue, shaking, sweating, and nausea.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"Cocaine is addictive even though the withdrawal symptoms are mild.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"Gambling can be a powerful addiction, even though no substance is withdrawn.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"Although both groups of rats pressed the lever, those that had self-administered heroin during the previous withdrawal state pressed more frequently.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"Users—rat or human—learn that the drug relieves the distress caused by drug withdrawal.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"The users then crave the drug during other kinds of distress.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"With other substances also, only some of the users develop an addiction.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"People with later onset are more likely to have reacted to life difficulties, less likely to have a family history of alcoholism, and more likely to respond well to treatment.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"After anyone drinks ethyl alcohol, enzymes in the liver metabolize it to acetaldehyde, a toxic substance.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"More than a third of the people in China and Japan have a gene that slows acetaldehyde metabolism.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"Probably for that reason, alcohol abuse has historically been uncommon in those countries.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"If so, it should be possible to monitor behavior of young people and predict their risk for later problems.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484},{"type":"bullet","text":"Other research follows this design: First, identify young men who are not yet problem drinkers.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484},{"type":"bullet","text":"If someone with strong intoxication from a moderate intake does develop an alcohol problem, it is usually less severe than that of other abusers.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484},{"type":"bullet","text":"The advice is, if you “hold your liquor well,” it is not something to brag about, but something to worry about.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484},{"type":"bullet","text":"Soon therapists tried using disulfiram as a drug, hoping that those with alcoholism would associate alcohol with illness and stop drinking.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485},{"type":"bullet","text":"When people take Antabuse, or a placebo that they think might be Antabuse, the threat of becoming ill strongly discourages any attempt to drink alcohol.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485},{"type":"bullet","text":"Heroin is an artificial substance invented in the 1800s as a supposedly safer alternative for people who were trying to quit morphine.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485},{"type":"bullet","text":"LAAM has the advantage of producing a longlasting effect so that the person visits a clinic three times a week instead of daily.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485},{"type":"bullet","text":"Calling addiction a disease helps to reduce some of the guilt and stigma.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486},{"type":"bullet","text":"As you have seen in this module, addiction does have a physiological basis.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486}],"topicIds":["bp14-m14-1-h01","bp14-m14-1-h02","bp14-m14-1-h03","bp14-m14-1-h04","bp14-m14-1-h05","bp14-m14-1-h06","bp14-m14-1-h07","bp14-m14-1-h08","bp14-m14-1-h09","bp14-m14-1-h10","bp14-m14-1-h11","bp14-m14-1-h12"],"studySections":[{"id":"bp14-m14-1-study-1","title":"Substance The reward-related role of dopamine is important but should not be translated into the simplistic claim that dopamine means pleasure or directly causes all addictions. Learning, expectation, environment, and stress influence the likelihood of seeking a substance. A substance-use problem involves persistent harmful patterns, not just the presence of a chemical in the body.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":462,"sourcePrintedEnd":469,"sourcePdfStart":480,"sourcePdfEnd":487},{"id":"bp14-m14-1-study-2","title":"Tolerance, withdrawal, and craving","text":"Tolerance describes a reduced response to a repeated dose or a need for more of a substance to produce a previous effect. Withdrawal refers to reactions that may occur when use is reduced or stopped after adaptation. Craving is a strong motivation or urge to use. These processes can occur together but are not interchangeable, and not all drugs produce identical patterns. Learned cues can trigger seeking even after acute withdrawal has passed, showing that addiction involves more than physical dependence.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":462,"sourcePrintedEnd":469,"sourcePdfStart":480,"sourcePdfEnd":487},{"id":"bp14-m14-1-study-3","title":"Why risk differs","text":"Genetic predispositions, environmental exposure, stress, learning history, and the specific pharmacological actions of a drug all contribute to risk. Studies of alcohol and opioid-related problems illustrate both shared and distinct mechanisms. A person's course cannot be predicted from one dopamine measurement or one family-history fact. Distinguish susceptibility from inevitability, and examine why certain settings increase the probability that drug use is repeated.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":462,"sourcePrintedEnd":469,"sourcePdfStart":480,"sourcePdfEnd":487},{"id":"bp14-m14-1-study-4","title":"Treatment principles","text":"Different treatments aim to reduce harmful use, manage withdrawal, block or substitute some drug effects, and change learned behavioral patterns. Medication and behavioral strategies can complement one another, depending on the substance and circumstances. Successful recovery often requires addressing social and environmental conditions as well as neural adaptation. the rats had an opportunity to press a lever to try to get heroin, but this time, the lever was inoperative.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":48},{"text":"Evidently, receiving an addictive drug during a withdrawal period is a powerful experience.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":49},{"text":"Although both groups of rats pressed the lever, those that had self-administered heroin during the previous withdrawal state pressed more frequently.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":124},{"text":"Users—rat or human—learn that the drug relieves the distress caused by drug withdrawal.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":125},{"text":"The users then crave the drug during other kinds of distress.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":126}],"originalFacts":5,"additionalFacts":3,"glossary":[{"term":"Withdrawal","definition":"effects of drug cessation","sourcePrintedPage":635,"sourcePdfPage":653}],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":159,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":150},{"id":"bp14-m14-1-h06","title":"Predispositions","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"facts":[{"text":"Most people drink alcohol in moderation, but others develop a habit of abuse.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":51},{"text":"Even among mice, some develop compulsive alcohol use when given the opportunity, and some do not .","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":52},{"text":"A great deal of the predisposition depends on experience.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":53},{"text":"People who had abusive experiences in childhood are more vulnerable, as is a child whose mother drank too much alcohol during pregnancy .","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":54},{"text":"Children who grew up without careful parental supervision are more likely to develop impulse problems than children of more attentive parents .","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":55},{"text":"As a rule, people with early-onset alcoholism (before age 25) have a family history of alcoholism, a genetic predisposition, and a rapid onset of the problem.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":56},{"text":"With other substances also, only some of the users develop an addiction.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":127},{"text":"People with later onset are more likely to have reacted to life difficulties, less likely to have a family history of alcoholism, and more likely to respond well to treatment.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":128}],"originalFacts":6,"additionalFacts":2,"glossary":[],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":186,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":152},{"id":"bp14-m14-1-h07","title":"Genetic Influences","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-1-h06","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"facts":[{"text":"The probability of abusing alcohol or other drugs also relates to genetic influences.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":58},{"text":"Parents’ alcohol use correlates more strongly with that of their biological children than their adopted children .","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":59},{"text":"Several genes affect the probability of substance use, with effects that vary from one environment to another .","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":60},{"text":"Most of these genes are non-specific, increasing the risk of several mental disorders, and risk-taking behaviors in general .","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":61},{"text":"One gene with a well-confirmed influence on alcohol abuse controls the metabolism of alcohol.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":62},{"text":"In fact, this is the only case of a common gene with a substantial effect on a human psychological disorder (other than Huntington’s disease).","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":63},{"text":"People with a gene that produces less acetaldehyde dehydrogenase metabolize acetaldehyde more slowly.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":64},{"text":"If they drink much alcohol, they accumulate acetaldehyde, which produces flushing of the face, increased heart rate, nausea, headache, abdominal pain, impaired breathing, and tissue damage.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":65},{"text":"After anyone drinks ethyl alcohol, enzymes in the liver metabolize it to acetaldehyde, a toxic substance.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":129},{"text":"More than a third of the people in China and Japan have a gene that slows acetaldehyde metabolism.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":130},{"text":"Probably for that reason, alcohol abuse has historically been uncommon in those countries.","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":131}],"originalFacts":8,"additionalFacts":3,"glossary":[{"term":"Huntington’s abuse, presumably the predisposition alters behavioral reactions to the substance.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":67},{"text":"By the time someone has developed a serious substance abuse problem, overcoming it is difficult.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":68},{"text":"Such studies find that alcoholism is more likely among those who were described in childhood as impulsive, risk taking, easily bored, sensation seeking, and outgoing .","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":69},{"text":"Because of the strong familial tendency toward alcoholism, researchers expect that many of the sons of alcoholics are future alcoholics themselves.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":70},{"text":"The most robust finding is that most sons of alcoholics show less than average intoxication after drinking a moderate amount of alcohol.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":71},{"text":"Presumably, someone who starts feeling tipsy after a couple of drinks stops at that point.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":72},{"text":"Follow-up studies found that men who report low intoxication after moderate drinking are more likely than others to develop an alcohol abuse problem .","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":73},{"text":"If so, it should be possible to monitor behavior of young people and predict their risk for later problems.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":132},{"text":"Other research follows this design: First, identify young men who are not yet problem drinkers.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":133},{"text":"If someone with strong intoxication from a moderate intake does develop an alcohol problem, it is usually less severe than that of other abusers.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":134},{"text":"The advice is, if you “hold your liquor well,” it is not something to brag about, but something to worry about.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":135}],"originalFacts":7,"additionalFacts":4,"glossary":[],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":411,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":226},{"id":"bp14-m14-1-h09","title":"Treatments","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"facts":[{"text":"Research has revealed much about the mechanisms of addiction.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":75},{"text":"Unfortunately, our increased understanding has not yet translated into better forms of treatment .","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":76},{"text":"In fact, that is the case for psychopathology in general.","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":77},{"text":"Research over recent decades has learned much about the genes, neurotransmitters, and other biological","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":78},{"text":"factors related to disorders, but treatment outcomes have not improved noticeably .","printedPage":467,"pdfPage":485,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"The most common treatment for substance abuse, especially in the United States, is participation in Alcoholics Anonymous, Narcotics Anonymous, or similar organizations.","printedPage":467,"pdfPage":485,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":80},{"text":"A smaller number of people consult a psychotherapist.","printedPage":467,"pdfPage":485,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":81},{"text":"Not many people turn to medications, but a few options are ineffective, but Antabuse is a special case because of why it is similar to the placebo.","printedPage":467,"pdfPage":485,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":86},{"text":"Antabuse is about equal to placebo not because Antabuse is ineffective, but because thinking that a placebo might be Antabuse makes the placebo effective .","printedPage":467,"pdfPage":485,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":87},{"text":"A related idea is to have people drink alcohol and then immediately take a drug that produces nausea, thereby forming a learned aversion to the taste of the alcohol.","printedPage":467,"pdfPage":485,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":88},{"text":"That procedure usually produces quick and effective avoidance of alcohol, although its use has never been popular .","printedPage":467,"pdfPage":485,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":89},{"text":"Other those with alcoholism would associate alcohol with illness and stop drinking.","printedPage":467,"pdfPage":485,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":136},{"text":"When people take Antabuse, or a placebo that they think might be Antabuse, the threat of becoming ill strongly discourages any attempt to drink adaptation with repeated exposure and life circumstances that promote continued use. Dependence, tolerance and a substance use disorder should not be treated as exact synonyms.","paragraphIndex":20011},{"label":"Tolerance","explanation":"After repeated exposure, the same dose may have less effect, or a larger amount may be required to obtain a familiar effect. Adaptation can differ across particular drug effects.","paragraphIndex":78106},{"label":"Withdrawal","explanation":"When adapted systems no longer receive the substance, uncomfortable or harmful reactions may emerge. Avoidance of withdrawal can become an additional reason for continued use.","paragraphIndex":78107}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Tolerance and withdrawal are consequences of repeated exposure, although they do not perfectly predict whether a person will develop addiction.","followUpParagraphIndex":45403,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h05","title":"Drug Use for Stress Reduction","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-1-h01","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"explanation":"People may initially use a substance to dampen anxiety or stress, creating a powerful cycle when the relief is temporary.","paragraphIndex":20012,"bullets":[{"label":"Negative reinforcement","explanation":"If using a drug removes an unpleasant state, that relief can reinforce repeated use even without strong pleasure.","paragraphIndex":20013},{"label":"Long-term problem","explanation":"As adaptation and stress accumulate, the same substance may become part of the source of distress it was used to reduce.","paragraphIndex":20014},{"label":"Negative reinforcement","explanation":"If using a drug reduces a distressing state, that relief can increase the chance of using it again in similar circumstances.","paragraphIndex":78108},{"label":"Cycle of dependence","explanation":"Stress and withdrawal-related distress can become triggers for renewed use. Treatment must consider the person's environment as well as the pharmacology of the substance.","paragraphIndex":78109}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Substance use may become a learned attempt to manage stress or negative emotion. Short-term relief can strengthen a behavior that creates longer-term difficulties.","followUpParagraphIndex":45404,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h06","title":"Predispositions","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"explanation":"Risk of problematic substance use reflects a mixture of personal and environmental influences. A predisposition increases probability; it does not make the outcome inevitable.","paragraphIndex":20015,"bullets":[{"label":"Multiple pathways","explanation":"Impulsivity, stress exposure, access to substances, learning history and vulnerability to reward cues can combine in different ways.","paragraphIndex":20016},{"label":"Protective influences","explanation":"Changes in circumstance, support and behavior can alter a person's trajectory even when some underlying risks remain.","paragraphIndex":20017},{"label":"Multiple influences","explanation":"Family history, early life, patterns of impulsive behavior, and availability of substances may change the probability of problematic use.","paragraphIndex":78110},{"label":"Avoid determinism","explanation":"A predisposition is not a prediction for one individual. Social setting, opportunities, and protective factors also matter.","paragraphIndex":78111}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Not everyone exposed to an addictive substance follows the same trajectory. Vulnerability reflects interacting personal characteristics, circumstances, and experiences.","followUpParagraphIndex":45405,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h07","title":"Genetic Influences","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-1-h06","printedPage":465,"pdfPage":483,"explanation":"Genetic studies find inherited contributions to vulnerability, but no single gene determines substance abuse. Genes can influence both the response to drugs and traits related to repeated use.","paragraphIndex":20018,"bullets":[{"label":"Indirect effects","explanation":"Inherited variation may affect metabolism, subjective drug effects, impulsivity or susceptibility to stress.","paragraphIndex":20019},{"label":"Interpretation","explanation":"A family resemblance can reflect shared genes and shared environment; useful studies attempt to separate these contributions.","paragraphIndex":20020},{"label":"Heritability evidence","explanation":"Resemblance between biological relatives can exceed resemblance between people raised together without genetic relationship for some patterns of substance use.","paragraphIndex":78112},{"label":"Gene–environment interaction","explanation":"A genetic influence can affect broad traits such as risk taking, and its effects depend on the environment. There is no one gene that determines addiction.","paragraphIndex":78113}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Studies of families, twins, and adopted children support genetic contributions to differences in substance-use risk, but the effect is spread across many factors.","followUpParagraphIndex":45406,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h08","title":"Behavioral Predictors of Abuse","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-1-h06","printedPage":466,"pdfPage":484,"explanation":"Behavioral tendencies can predict risk without explaining it completely. Researchers examine traits that appear before heavy substance use to avoid mistaking consequences for causes.","paragraphIndex":20021,"bullets":[{"label":"Individual differences","explanation":"Novelty seeking, response to reward or difficulty inhibiting behavior may make particular patterns of use more likely.","paragraphIndex":20022},{"label":"Avoid overprediction","explanation":"Many people with a risk factor never develop problematic use, while others develop it without obvious early markers.","paragraphIndex":20023},{"label":"Behavioral prediction","explanation":"Researchers examine how traits measured before substantial use relate to later outcomes.","paragraphIndex":78114},{"label":"Interpretation","explanation":"A predictor is not necessarily a direct cause. Multiple pathways can lead to the same outcome, so a person's behavior should not be treated as an irreversible destiny.","paragraphIndex":78115}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Certain early behavioral patterns predict elevated risk of later substance problems, but prediction is probabilistic. These notes describe the textbook, not personal treatment advice.","paragraphIndex":78117}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Treatment addresses biological adaptation, learned habits, stress, and the person's social context. Medication is one component rather than a substitute for support.","paragraphIndex":20027,"bullets":[{"label":"Different targets","explanation":"Some approaches make drinking aversive; others reduce the reinforcement or urge associated with alcohol.","paragraphIndex":20028},{"label":"Clinical principle","explanation":"Treatment choice depends on the person's medical situation and goals; this textbook explains biological mechanisms, not an instruction to self-medicate.","paragraphIndex":20029},{"label":"Different targets","explanation":"Some medications discourage drinking through physiological reactions; others influence systems involved in reinforcement or craving.","paragraphIndex":78118},{"label":"Clinical significance","explanation":"Evidence and suitability vary. This can reduce unstable cycles of intoxication and withdrawal.","paragraphIndex":20030,"bullets":[{"label":"Agonist approaches","explanation":"A medically managed, longer-acting substitute can stabilize receptor activity and reduce withdrawal and unsafe behavior.","paragraphIndex":20031},{"label":"Antagonist approaches","explanation":"Blocking opioid effects can decrease reinforcement for some patients. Selection and timing require professional assessment because effects and withdrawal risks differ.","paragraphIndex":20032},{"label":"Agonist and antagonist logic","explanation":"Longer-acting receptor stimulation can reduce cycles of intoxication and withdrawal; receptor blockade can prevent some effects of subsequently used opioids.","paragraphIndex":78120},{"label":"Why supervision matters","explanation":"These approaches differ in their requirements, limitations, and risks. The chapter's discussion is explanatory rather than instructions for choosing or using a medication.","paragraphIndex":78121}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Medications for opioid-use problems can act on opioid receptors to reduce withdrawal, limit intoxication, or block the effects of opioids.
