Disorders","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":470,"printedEnd":480,"pdfStart":488,"pdfEnd":498,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Major depressive disorder and bipolar disorder involve persistent disturbances in mood and functioning, not simply ordinary emotional responses. The text reviews genetic and stress-related influences alongside biological treatments."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Compare standard antidepressants, proposed mechanisms for delayed effects, psychedelics under investigation, non-drug approaches, and treatments for bipolar disorder. Notice the limits and variability of treatment response."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-2-study-1","text":"Major depressive disorder"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Major depressive disorder involves persistent changes in mood or interest accompanied by additional cognitive, bodily, and behavioral symptoms that cause meaningful impairment. It should not be equated with a brief period of ordinary sadness. Biological research examines predispositions involving genetic variation, stress, pain, and changes in neural systems, while recognizing that none is a definitive cause for every individual. The condition is heterogeneous, so two people can meet diagnostic criteria with partly different symptom patterns."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-2-study-2","text":"Antidepressants and mechanism questions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Several established antidepressants alter monoamine-related signaling, including serotonin or norepinephrine systems. Their clinical effects generally unfold over time, which suggests that immediate transmitter changes are not the whole explanation. Researchers investigate later changes in neural plasticity and system regulation. It is not accurate to teach depression as simply 'too little serotonin' or imply that raising one transmitter immediately eliminates its causes. Drug effectiveness must be evaluated against placebo response, variability, and side effects."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-2-study-3","text":"Other approaches and ongoing questions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Non-drug treatments and biological interventions may be useful in different circumstances. The chapter considers evidence for alternatives to conventional antidepressants and research into psychedelics as potential treatments. Promising findings need to be distinguished from broad clinical approval or guaranteed outcomes. Combining symptom relief with sustained coping and functioning is the meaningful goal, and treatment choice depends on individual needs and professional assessment."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-2-study-4","text":"Bipolar disorder is distinct"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Bipolar disorder involves episodes of abnormally elevated or irritable mood and altered energy, often alongside depressive periods. It is not simply rapid ordinary mood swings. The biology and treatment considerations differ in important ways from major depression, so a drug used for one diagnosis may not be appropriate in the same way for another. For revision, contrast the clinical features, predispositions, and treatment logic rather than grouping every mood change under a single heading."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h01","text":"Major Depressive Disorder"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with major depression feel sad and helpless most of the day every day for weeks at a time (Figure 14.5).","sourcePrintedPage":470,"sourcePdfPage":488,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cognitive limitations often persist even after successful treatment of the mood problems .","sourcePrintedPage":470,"sourcePdfPage":488,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"an average number of unpleasant experiences but far below the average number of pleasant ones .","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with depression reacted normally to sad or frightening depictions but seldom smiled at the comedies or pleasant pictures .","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In addition to the lack of pleasure, depression is marked by “negative bias,” a tendency to interpret events in a discouraging way.","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Almost everyone with depression has sleep problems, which generally precede the mood changes .","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In most cases, people have episodes of depression separated by periods of normal mood.","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Several studies reported that the early episodes were longer, and that later episodes were briefer but more frequent .","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That will include anyone who ever became depressed, including some who had just one episode lasting many years.","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h02","text":"Genetics"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Studies of twins and adopted children indicate a moderate degree of heritability for depression .","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As with substance abuse, heritability is higher for early-onset depression than for depression later in life .","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have identified at least 17 common genetic variants linked to depression , each with small effects.","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A study of Chinese women with recurrent severe depression identified two genes with a strong effect.","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Those genes did not emerge in studies on Europeans, simply because those genes are rare in Europe .","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One research problem is that when we talk about depression, we are probably combining two or more syndromes.","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An influential study reported that one genetic variant related to serotonin reuptake increased the risk of depression only for people with a history of major stressful experiences .","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"This was an exciting idea, but later results were inconsistent, and the largest attempt to replicate it found no support for the hypothesis .","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h03","text":"Pain and Stress"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although a genetic predisposition can make depression more likely, events in the environment are the immediate triggers.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Pain is so closely associated with depression that some languages use the same word for both.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Pain decreases the activity of dopamine neurons that are important for both motivation and reward .","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Depression often occurs in women shortly after giving birth, or around the time of menopause, events that put much strain on the body.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most of the women who experience depression at those times had previous bouts of depression, and the stress of delivery or menopause triggered a recurrence .","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many of the cytokines released by the immune system produce inflammation, and many people with depression show signs of brain inflammation .","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h04","text":"Antidepressant Drugs"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One insight into possible biological bases of depression comes from research on drugs that relieve it.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"You might assume that investigators first determine the causes of a psychological disorder and then develop medications based on the causes.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The opposite has been more common: Investigators find drugs that seem helpful, and then they try to understand how the drugs work.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Iproniazid, the first antidepressant drug, was originally marketed to treat tuberculosis, until physicians noticed that it relieved depression.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Chlorpromazine was originally used as a tranquilizer, until physicians noticed its ability to alleviate schizophrenia.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Today, researchers start by testing drugs in test tubes or tissue samples, in order to use fewer laboratory animals.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h05","text":"Standard Antidepressants"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Antidepressant drugs include tricyclics, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and atypical antidepressants.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The tricyclics (e.g., imipramine, trade name Tofranil) operate by blocking the transporter proteins that reabsorb serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine into the presynaptic neuron after their release.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A tricyclic drug locks the transporter into its initial position and blocks reuptake, thus prolonging the presence of the neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft .","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Blocking histamine produces drowsiness, blocking acetylcholine leads to dry mouth and difficulty urinating, and blocking sodium channels causes heart irregularities.","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, researchers have reported that a combination of drugs increases the number of side effects without demonstrably improving the antidepressant response .","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The MAOIs were the earliest antidepressants, but today physicians prescribe them only for patients who did not respond to other antidepressants.","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People taking MAOIs must avoid foods containing tyramine—including cheese, raisins, and many others—because a combination of tyramine and MAOIs increases blood pressure.","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One example is bupropion (Wellbutrin), which inhibits the reuptake of dopamine and to some extent norepinephrine.","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because it is a nutritional supplement instead of a drug, the U.S.","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"John’s wort increases the effectiveness of a liver enzyme that breaks down plant toxins, and also breaks down most medicines.","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h06","text":"How Do Antidepressants Act?"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When researchers discovered antidepressants that increase the availability of serotonin and other neurotransmitters, they at first assumed that the cause of depression was a deficiency of serotonin or other neurotransmitters.","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Procedures that suddenly decrease serotonin levels do not provoke feelings of depression in most people .","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most importantly, the time course does not fit: Antidepressants reach the brain within minutes to hours, but people generally need to take the drugs for at least 2 weeks before they experience noticeable benefits .","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Depression is associated with decreased levels of the neurotrophin called brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), which is important for synaptic plasticity and learning .","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, because they do not bind strongly to that receptor, they have to accumulate for weeks to reach a high enough brain concentration to produce a significant effect .","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A mutation in the receptor for BDNF prevents antidepressants from exerting their effects .","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h07","text":"How Effective Are Antidepressants?"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Not everyone is convinced , and we must at least say that their effectiveness is limited.","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most controlled studies find that antidepressants are at least moderately more effective than placebos, but even when the advantage over placebos is statistically significant, it is not always strong in a clinical sense .","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The horizontal axis represents scores on the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale at the start of treatment, where higher scores indicate more intense depression.","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Triangles represent patients receiving the drug in a study, and circles represent patients receiving a placebo.","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The size of the triangle or circle is proportional to the number of patients in a group.","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many people respond well on placebos, either because of spontaneous recovery over time or because of the expectation that comes from taking a pill.","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, these data probably understate the effectiveness of the drugs at lower levels of depression, where the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale has lower reliability and validity .","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When people take antidepressants, many fail to show a benefit from the first drug they try.","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Controlled studies find little evidence that different doses of SSRIs produce different effects .","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h08","text":"Psychedelics as Medications"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In the 1950s and 1960s, several psychotherapists reported successful results from using psychedelics to aid treatments—that is, drugs that distort perception.","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The scientific quality of the early research was weak, and the drugs developed a bad reputation for several reasons.","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Decades later, research resumed, finding that LSD or psilocybin can help relieve depression, anxiety, PTSD, and substance abuse.","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"of the difficulty of doing a placebo-controlled study. (People know whether they took the drug or the placebo because a placebo produces no psychedelic effects.) Still, the benefits appear to be real in many cases, developing faster than those of other drugs and lasting for weeks or months.","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Unlike the standard antidepressant drugs, the psychedelics must be administered in a therapeutic session with careful supervision, to avoid serious risks.","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A typical protocol is a 4- to 5-hour session of relaxation under the psychedelic influence, followed by a discussion with a therapist the next day, and then a second session later .","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Evidently, the hallucinogenic effects depend mostly on one site and the antidepressant effects depend mostly on another site, and therefore it may be possible to develop new drugs with the benefits of the psychedelics, but with less risk .","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h09","text":"Alternatives to Medication"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain scans show that psychotherapy and antidepressants increase metabolism in the same brain areas .","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If mental activity is the same thing as brain activity, then changing thoughts and changing brain chemistry are the same thing.","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"On average, people receiving both treatments show more rapid improvement than people receiving either one alone, but the percentage of people showing improvement increases only slightly .","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Electroconvulsive Therapy and Brain Stimulation Another option, despite its stormy history, is treatment through an electrically induced seizure, known as electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) .","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Insulin shock is a dreadful experience, however, and difficult to control.","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, its misuse during the 1950s earned it a bad reputation when some patients were given ECT hundreds of times without their consent.","sourcePrintedPage":476,"sourcePdfPage":494,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Nearly a century after the introduction of ECT, no one is yet sure how it relieves depression, but like antidepressant drugs, ECT increases BDNF levels and increases the proliferation of new neurons in the hippocampus .","sourcePrintedPage":476,"sourcePdfPage":494,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Exercise and Sleep The simplest and least expensive antidepressant treatment is a program of moderate-intensity exercise.","sourcePrintedPage":476,"sourcePdfPage":494,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Exercise increases blood flow to the brain and increases the supply of nutrition to the brain.","sourcePrintedPage":476,"sourcePdfPage":494,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Eventually, however, the circadian rhythm shifts again, as if the person had traveled west again.","sourcePrintedPage":476,"sourcePdfPage":494,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Phaseadvancing the sleep schedule has not become a popular therapy, because people have social reasons for wanting to stay awake after early evening.","sourcePrintedPage":476,"sourcePdfPage":494,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast to most other patients with depression, who have phase-advanced circadian rhythms, people with seasonal affective disorder have phase-delayed rhythms (Figure 14.11).","sourcePrintedPage":476,"sourcePdfPage":494,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h10","text":"Bipolar Disorder"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Mania is characterized by restless activity, excitement, excessive self-confidence, rambling speech, and loss of inhibitions.","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with fullfledged manic episodes have bipolar I disorder , and those with only mild, hypomanic episodes have bipolar II disorder .","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Bipolar disorder usually has its onset in the teenage years or early 20s.","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"At least 30 common genetic variants are linked to bipolar disorder, although no common variant has a large effect.","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some of the genes linked to bipolar disorder also show a slightly positive correlation with creative accomplishments in acting, art, music, or writing .","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In addition to genetics, a history of childhood maltreatment also increases the risk of bipolar disorder .","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h11","text":"Treatments"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The first successful treatment for bipolar disorder, and still the most common one, is lithium salts.","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cade mixed uric acid (a component of urine) with a lithium salt to help it dissolve and then gave the solution to patients.","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It was indeed helpful, but investigators soon discovered that lithium was the effective agent, not uric acid.","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The dose must be regulated carefully, as a low dose is ineffective, and a high dose is toxic.","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Bipolar disorder is associated with overactivity of mitochondria, leading to hyperactivity of many neurons.","sourcePrintedPage":477,"sourcePdfPage":495,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Patients with bipolar disorder frequently have poor sleep quality during manic phases, depressed phases, and even when their mood is normal .","sourcePrintedPage":478,"sourcePdfPage":496,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-2-h12","text":"In Closing: The Biology of Mood Swings"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"There is nothing abnormal about feeling sad after a bad experience.","sourcePrintedPage":478,"sourcePdfPage":496,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For people with major depression or bipolar disorder, mood becomes largely independent of events.","sourcePrintedPage":478,"sourcePdfPage":496,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Depression persists despite good news, and mania produces self-confidence that no contradiction can deter.","sourcePrintedPage":478,"sourcePdfPage":496,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Studying these states informs us about the brain states that correspond to moods.","sourcePrintedPage":478,"sourcePdfPage":496,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Getting consistent, adequate sleep helps stabilize mood and decrease the risk of a new episode .","sourcePrintedPage":478,"sourcePdfPage":496,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They’re also presented in alphabetical order with definitions in the book’s Subject Index/Glossary at the end of this book.","sourcePrintedPage":478,"sourcePdfPage":496,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some people have suggested that ECT relieves depression by causing people to forget the events that caused it.","sourcePrintedPage":479,"sourcePdfPage":497,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Measurements from the nucleus accumbens show less response to reward.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":470,"sourcePdfPage":488},{"type":"bullet","text":"In one study, people carried a beeper that sounded at unpredictable times to signal them to describe their emotional reactions.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":470,"sourcePdfPage":488},{"type":"bullet","text":"In other studies, people examined photographs or films as researchers recorded their reactions.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489},{"type":"bullet","text":"A later analysis showed that these reports reflected a statistical artifact: Suppose you measure the mean length of all first episodes.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489},{"type":"bullet","text":"To have that many episodes, each of them had to be brief.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489},{"type":"bullet","text":"If you compare the length of, say, first and fifth episodes but include only people who had at least five episodes, the mean lengths are about the same.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489},{"type":"bullet","text":"People with early-onset depression (before age 30) have a high probability of having other relatives with psychiatric problems, not always depression.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489},{"type":"bullet","text":"People with lateonset depression (especially after age 45 to 50) have a high probability of relatives with circulatory problems.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":471,"sourcePdfPage":489},{"type":"bullet","text":"The immune system releases proteins called cytokines that fight an infection and conserve energy by reducing activity levels and decreasing appetite.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490},{"type":"bullet","text":"Inflammation impairs the activity of mitochondria, resulting in decreased energy, another symptom of depression.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490},{"type":"bullet","text":"For decades, researchers evaluated drugs just by trial and error.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h04","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490},{"type":"bullet","text":"The illustration shows how the serotonin transporter protein picks up a serotonin molecule outside the membrane and then flips to deliver the molecule inside the neuron.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490},{"type":"bullet","text":"People need to limit their use of tricyclic drugs to minimize these side effects.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490},{"type":"bullet","text":"Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) attach to the center of just the serotonin transporter protein and lock it into a shape that blocks serotonin from binding to it.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490},{"type":"bullet","text":"Perhaps surprisingly, antidepressants that target different neurotransmitters are about equally effective.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":472,"sourcePdfPage":490},{"type":"bullet","text":"The monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) (e.g., phenelzine, trade name Nardil) block monoamine oxidase (MAO), a presynaptic enzyme that breaks catecholamines and serotonin into inactive forms.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491},{"type":"bullet","text":"When MAOIs block this enzyme, the presynaptic terminal has more of its transmitter available for release.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491},{"type":"bullet","text":"John’s wort decreases the effectiveness of other drugs you might be taking—antidepressant drugs, cancer drugs, AIDS drugs, and others.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491},{"type":"bullet","text":"As a result of low BDNF, depression is associated with impaired learning.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h06","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491},{"type":"bullet","text":"Standard antidepressants attach to a receptor for BDNF and facilitate its release.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h06","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491},{"type":"bullet","text":"So far, we have considered explanations of how antidepressants work.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h07","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492},{"type":"bullet","text":"Figure 14.9 summarizes the results of many experiments in which people were randomly assigned to antidepressant drugs or placebos.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h07","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492},{"type":"bullet","text":"For patients with mild to moderate depression, the differences between the drug group and the placebo group appear too small to be meaningful.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h07","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492},{"type":"bullet","text":"After a few weeks, the psychiatrist might prescribe a different drug, and then perhaps another one, and so forth, on a trial-and-error process.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h07","sourcePrintedPage":474,"sourcePdfPage":492},{"type":"bullet","text":"In addition to effects on serotonin synapses, these drugs enhance neural plasticity, just used ketamine could not safely drive home, for example.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h08","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493},{"type":"bullet","text":"Cognitive behavioral therapy and other forms of psychotherapy produce benefits that are about equal to the effects of antidepressant last.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h09","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493},{"type":"bullet","text":"ECT originated with the observation that if someone had both epilepsy and schizophrenia, when symptoms of one disorder increase, symptoms of the other often decrease.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h09","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493},{"type":"bullet","text":"In the 1930s, Ladislas Meduna and other physicians tried to relieve schizophrenia by inducing convulsions with a large dose of insulin.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h09","sourcePrintedPage":475,"sourcePdfPage":493},{"type":"bullet","text":"When antidepressant drugs became available in the late 1950s, the use of ECT declined respond to the drugs.","headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h09","sourcePrintedPage":476,"sourcePdfPage":494},{"type":"bullet","text":"Another option is certainly not the first thing you would try, but it is worth depressive disorder","text":"Major depressive disorder involves persistent changes in mood or interest accompanied by additional cognitive, bodily, and behavioral symptoms that cause meaningful impairment. It should not be equated with a brief period of ordinary sadness. Biological research examines predispositions involving genetic variation, stress, pain, and changes in neural systems, while recognizing that none is a definitive cause for every individual. The condition is heterogeneous, so two people can meet diagnostic criteria with partly different symptom patterns.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":470,"sourcePrintedEnd":480,"sourcePdfStart":488,"sourcePdfEnd":498},{"id":"bp14-m14-2-study-2","title":"Antidepressants and mechanism questions","text":"Several established antidepressants alter monoamine-related signaling, including serotonin or norepinephrine systems. Their clinical effects generally unfold over time, which suggests that immediate transmitter changes are not the whole explanation. Researchers investigate later changes in neural plasticity and system regulation. It is not accurate to teach depression as simply 'too little serotonin' or imply that raising one transmitter immediately eliminates its causes. Drug effectiveness must be evaluated against placebo response, variability, and side effects.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":470,"sourcePrintedEnd":480,"sourcePdfStart":488,"sourcePdfEnd":498},{"id":"bp14-m14-2-study-3","title":"Other approaches and ongoing questions","text":"Non-drug treatments and biological interventions may be useful in different circumstances. The chapter considers evidence for alternatives to conventional antidepressants and research into psychedelics as potential treatments. It is not simply rapid ordinary mood swings. The biology and treatment considerations differ in important ways from major depression, so a drug used for one diagnosis may not be appropriate in the same way for another. For revision, contrast the clinical features, predispositions, and treatment logic rather than grouping every mood change under a single heading.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":470,"sourcePrintedEnd":480,"sourcePdfStart":488,"sourcePdfEnd":498}],"contentLevel":"complete_sample_classroom_notes_plus_legacy_source_extraction","selfCheck":[{"question":"Can you explain: Major depressive disorder?","answer":"Major depressive disorder involves persistent changes in mood or interest accompanied by additional cognitive, bodily, and behavioral symptoms that cause meaningful impairment. It should not be equated with a brief period of ordinary sadness. Biological research examines predispositions involving genetic variation, stress, pain, and changes in neural systems, while recognizing that none is a definitive cause for every individual. The condition is heterogeneous, so two people can meet diagnostic criteria with partly different symptom patterns."},{"question":"Can you explain: Antidepressants and mechanism questions?","answer":"Several established antidepressants alter monoamine-related signaling, including serotonin or norepinephrine systems. Their clinical effects generally unfold over time, which suggests that immediate transmitter changes are not the whole explanation. Researchers investigate later changes in neural plasticity and system regulation. It is not accurate to teach depression as simply 'too little serotonin' or imply that raising one transmitter immediately eliminates its causes. Drug effectiveness must be evaluated against placebo response, variability, and side effects."},{"question":"Can you explain: Other approaches and ongoing questions?","answer":"Non-drug treatments and biological interventions may be useful in different circumstances. The chapter considers evidence for alternatives to conventional antidepressants and research into psychedelics as potential treatments. Promising findings need to be distinguished from broad clinical approval or guaranteed outcomes. Combining symptom relief with sustained coping and functioning is the meaningful goal, and treatment choice depends on individual needs and professional assessment."},{"question":"Can you explain: Bipolar disorder is distinct?","answer":"Bipolar disorder involves episodes of abnormally elevated or irritable mood and altered energy, often alongside depressive periods. It is not simply rapid ordinary mood swings. The biology and treatment considerations differ in important ways from major depression, so a drug used for one diagnosis may not be appropriate in the same way for another. .","printedPage":471,"pdfPage":489,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":25},{"text":"One research problem is that when we talk about depression, we are .","printedPage":471,"pdfPage":489,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":27},{"text":"This was an exciting idea, but later results were inconsistent, and .","printedPage":471,"pdfPage":489,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":28},{"text":"People with early-onset depression (before age 30) have a high .","printedPage":472,"pdfPage":490,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":34},{"text":"Many of the cytokines released by the immune system produce .","printedPage":472,"pdfPage":490,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":35},{"text":"The immune system releases proteins called cytokines that fight an .","printedPage":475,"pdfPage":493,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":78},{"text":"In addition to effects on serotonin synapses, these drugs enhance .","printedPage":475,"pdfPage":493,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":82},{"text":"Electroconvulsive Therapy and Brain Stimulation Another option, .","printedPage":475,"pdfPage":493,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":83},{"text":"Insulin shock is a dreadful experience, however, and difficult to .","printedPage":476,"pdfPage":494,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":86},{"text":"Exercise and Sleep The simplest and least expensive antidepressant brain.","printedPage":476,"pdfPage":494,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":88},{"text":"Eventually, however, the circadian rhythm shifts again, as if that go beyond ordinary sadness after a disappointment. The textbook considers biological vulnerability alongside stress and experience.","paragraphIndex":20000,"bullets":[{"label":"More than feeling low","explanation":"Disturbances may include loss of pleasure, sleep and appetite changes, low energy, reduced concentration and harmful thoughts.","paragraphIndex":20001},{"label":"Clinical distinction","explanation":"Duration, breadth and functional impairment matter; no single symptom or neurotransmitter measurement is sufficient to diagnose a person.","paragraphIndex":20002},{"label":"Clinical pattern","explanation":"The combination, duration, and interference of symptoms are more informative than one isolated feeling. Loss of interest or pleasure may be prominent.","paragraphIndex":78200},{"label":"Biological perspective","explanation":"Altered responses in circuits associated with motivation and emotion are among the findings studied. Brain-level observations do not reduce the person's experience to a single chemical imbalance.","paragraphIndex":78201}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Major depressive disorder goes beyond ordinary short periods of sadness. It involves persistent mood changes together with effects on motivation, thinking, sleep, appetite, and daily functioning.","followUpParagraphIndex":49400,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h02","title":"Genetics","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-2-h01","printedPage":471,"pdfPage":489,"explanation":"Depression runs in families partly because inherited factors shape vulnerability, but the genetics are complex and overlap with other psychiatric conditions.","paragraphIndex":20003,"bullets":[{"label":"Polygenic risk","explanation":"Many genetic variants contribute small effects rather than one dominant depression gene.","paragraphIndex":20004},{"label":"Gene–environment relation","explanation":"Inborn vulnerability may change how a person responds to stress; the same stressful event does not lead everyone to the same outcome.","paragraphIndex":20005},{"label":"Magnitude and context","explanation":"The contribution differs across age of onset and populations; heritability is not a certainty for one person.","paragraphIndex":78202},{"label":"Interpretation","explanation":"A biological predisposition can change susceptibility without fixing when or whether a depressive episode occurs. Environmental stressors remain important.","paragraphIndex":78203}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Family, twin, and adoption evidence indicates a genetic contribution to depression, but genetic risk is distributed and interacts with life circumstances.","followUpParagraphIndex":49401,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h03","title":"Pain and Stress","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-2-h01","printedPage":472,"pdfPage":490,"explanation":"Painful experiences and prolonged stress can contribute to depression through psychological and physiological pathways. The relationship is bidirectional, not a simple one-way cause.","paragraphIndex":20006,"bullets":[{"label":"Stress systems","explanation":"Repeated stress can alter hormonal and neural regulation of mood and motivation.","paragraphIndex":20007},{"label":"Chronic pain","explanation":"Pain can worsen depressive symptoms and depression can intensify the experience of pain; observing co-occurrence alone cannot identify the only direction of causality.","paragraphIndex":20008},{"label":"Stress systems","explanation":"Sustained stress affects nervous-system signaling and bodily regulation, offering pathways by which experiences can alter mood.","paragraphIndex":78204},{"label":"Complex causation","explanation":"No stressful event has the same impact on every person. History, support, predisposition, and how stress is interpreted all shape risk.","paragraphIndex":78205}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Stressful experiences and pain are closely related to depressive symptoms. The relationship may operate in both directions and through more than one biological mechanism.","followUpParagraphIndex":49402,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h04","title":"Antidepressant Drugs","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":472,"pdfPage":490,"explanation":"Antidepressant medicines affect signaling systems involved in mood, but their clinical benefits are not explained fully by the immediate increase or decrease of one transmitter.","paragraphIndex":20009,"bullets":[{"label":"Major groups","explanation":"Common medications alter monoamine transmission, often involving serotonin or norepinephrine, through different mechanisms.","paragraphIndex":20010},{"label":"Important delay","explanation":"Biochemical actions begin quickly, whereas meaningful mood improvement often takes longer, indicating that downstream adaptation and plasticity contribute.","paragraphIndex":20011},{"label":"Reverse inference","explanation":"Knowing that a drug changes a transmitter system and sometimes reduces symptoms does not prove that low levels of that transmitter caused the illness.","paragraphIndex":78206},{"label":"Clinical timing","explanation":"Changes in neural chemistry may begin before noticeable improvement, suggesting that later adaptation matters.","paragraphIndex":78207}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"The study of antidepressant drugs contributed to hypotheses about depression because treatments altered neurotransmission. The logic works from observed drug effects back toward possible mechanisms.","followUpParagraphIndex":49403,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h05","title":"Standard Antidepressants","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-2-h04","printedPage":472,"pdfPage":490,"explanation":"The standard drugs discussed include selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and other agents that affect transmitter availability. Each class has benefits, limitations and possible adverse effects.","paragraphIndex":20012,"bullets":[{"label":"Reuptake inhibition","explanation":"Blocking transporters can prolong transmitter availability at synapses; different drugs target different transporters or receptors.","paragraphIndex":20013},{"label":"Treatment trade-off","explanation":"Side effects, interactions and uneven response make monitoring and individualized clinical prescribing essential.","paragraphIndex":20014},{"label":"Major classes","explanation":"Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, tricyclic drugs, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and other antidepressants affect serotonin, norepinephrine, or related systems by different mechanisms.","paragraphIndex":78208},{"label":"Studying them","explanation":"Compare how they alter transmitter availability and how their limitations affect use, rather than memorizing brand names as though they explained the disorder.","paragraphIndex":78209}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Standard antidepressants include several groups with different effects on monoamine transmission. The most familiar classes are not identical in action or adverse effects.","followUpParagraphIndex":49404,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h06","title":"How Do Antidepressants Act?","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-2-h04","printedPage":473,"pdfPage":491,"explanation":"Researchers have questioned the claim that depression is simply caused by insufficient serotonin. The textbook contrasts immediate drug action with slower changes in neural functioning.","paragraphIndex":20015,"bullets":[{"label":"Timing problem","explanation":"A reuptake-blocking drug can alter synaptic conditions rapidly, while improvement commonly develops after repeated dosing.","paragraphIndex":20016},{"label":"Plasticity hypothesis","explanation":"Changes involving brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), receptor activity and synaptic adaptation may help explain delayed effects, though no single account covers all cases.","paragraphIndex":20017},{"label":"Immediate versus delayed","explanation":"Transporter or enzyme effects occur earlier than many changes in mood, implying downstream processes are involved.","paragraphIndex":78210},{"label":"Evidence check","explanation":"Lowering serotonin experimentally does not consistently induce depression in otherwise healthy participants. The drug response is informative but not a definitive account of causation.","paragraphIndex":78211}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"The delayed clinical effects of antidepressants challenge the simplest version of the chemical-imbalance explanation. Neuronal systems adapt after the initial pharmacological action.","followUpParagraphIndex":49405,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","masterclass":{"id":"bp14-m14-2-h06","points":[{"label":"Initial pharmacological effect","explanation":"Many antidepressants alter serotonin, norepinephrine, or related systems by affecting reuptake, metabolism, or receptor processes. These actions can occur relatively soon after a dose.","paragraphIndex":790301},{"label":"Clinical response is often delayed","explanation":"Improvement commonly develops over a longer period, indicating that downstream neural or behavioral adaptations matter beyond the earliest transmitter change.","paragraphIndex":790302},{"label":"Treatment efficacy is variable","explanation":"Controlled comparisons help show whether outcomes exceed placebo improvement, but differences vary by severity, study, medication, and individual response.","paragraphIndex":790303},{"label":"Other treatments and pathways","explanation":"Psychotherapy and other interventions can help some patients, so benefit cannot be reduced to the particular receptor mechanism of an antidepressant drug.","paragraphIndex":790304}],"explanation":"Antidepressant drugs provided crucial evidence that changes in neurotransmission can alter mood, but a drug's effective action does not establish that depression originally resulted from a deficiency of one chemical. The chapter uses this distinction to question overly simple biological explanations.","caution":"'Antidepressants affect serotonin' and 'low serotonin is the verified cause of every depression' are logically different claims.","checkQuestion":"Why would a lag between the drug's early receptor effects and later symptom improvement weaken a one-step chemical-imbalance theory?","title":"How Do Antidepressants Act?","sourcePrintedPage":473,"sourcePdfPage":491,"explanationIndex":790300,"cautionIndex":790345,"questionIndex":790346,"kind":"original_classroom_walkthrough","editorialStatus":"individually_written_source_grounded_explanation","depth":"extended","source":"Kalat Biological Psychology 14e uploaded PDF + existing source-grounded topic map","totalWords":178},"studyDepth":"guided_deep"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h07","title":"How Effective Are Antidepressants?","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-2-h04","printedPage":474,"pdfPage":492,"explanation":"Trials generally find benefits from antidepressant medication for some patients, but improvement varies widely and placebo comparison requires careful interpretation.","paragraphIndex":20018,"bullets":[{"label":"Statistical versus practical effect","explanation":"A difference can be statistically significant yet modest for a particular person's symptoms.","paragraphIndex":20019},{"label":"Clinical reality","explanation":"Some patients do not respond to the first medication and require reassessment; it is incorrect to present any one drug as universally effective.","paragraphIndex":20020},{"label":"Research method","explanation":"Randomized comparisons help separate the medication's contribution from expectation, natural changes in symptoms, and general care.","paragraphIndex":78212},{"label":"Interpretation","explanation":"A statistically detectable difference is not always a large improvement for everyday functioning. Severity, measures, side effects, and individual variability complicate conclusions.","paragraphIndex":78213}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Controlled comparisons often find an advantage for antidepressant medication over placebo, but the average size and clinical significance of the benefit vary.","followUpParagraphIndex":49406,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h08","title":"Psychedelics as Medications","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-2-h04","printedPage":474,"pdfPage":492,"explanation":"The textbook reviews renewed clinical research into psychedelic-assisted interventions and related rapidly acting approaches, while noting important methodological limits.","paragraphIndex":20021,"bullets":[{"label":"Study design","explanation":"Participants often notice whether they received a perception-altering substance, making blinding and placebo comparison difficult.","paragraphIndex":20022},{"label":"Caution","explanation":"Promising early findings are not permission for unsupervised use; benefits, safety and durability must be evaluated under appropriate clinical conditions.","paragraphIndex":20023},{"label":"Research quality","explanation":"Claims require controlled designs that examine expectancy effects, blinding, safety, and lasting outcomes.","paragraphIndex":78214},{"label":"Scope","explanation":"Promising findings in selected settings are not a reason to treat these substances as routine self-medication. Their psychological and physiological risks remain relevant.","paragraphIndex":78215}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"The textbook reviews renewed research on psychedelic substances as potential adjuncts to treatment. Early enthusiasm was followed by methodological concerns, making careful study especially important.","followUpParagraphIndex":49407,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h09","title":"Alternatives to Medication","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-2-h04","printedPage":475,"pdfPage":493,"explanation":"Psychotherapy and other interventions can change brain activity as well as thought and behavior. This challenges the false idea that psychological treatment is somehow separate from biology.","paragraphIndex":20024,"bullets":[{"label":"Psychotherapy","explanation":"Learning different interpretations and coping behaviors can produce measurable change in the neural systems that support mood.","paragraphIndex":20025},{"label":"Other interventions","explanation":"The chapter discusses electroconvulsive therapy, brain stimulation and sleep-related approaches for selected cases; their mechanisms, benefits and drawbacks differ.","paragraphIndex":20026},{"label":"Psychological interventions","explanation":"Psychotherapy can target patterns of thought, behavior, and coping, with effects that can be examined biologically.","paragraphIndex":78216},{"label":"Other interventions","explanation":"The text considers non-drug approaches, including methods that change brain activity more directly. Effectiveness and suitability should be evaluated by evidence rather than by assuming a 'natural' intervention is always safer.","paragraphIndex":78217}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Depression treatments also include approaches that work through experience and activity, not only medication. Changes in thought, behavior, and brain function are interconnected.","followUpParagraphIndex":49408,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h10","title":"Bipolar Disorder","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":477,"pdfPage":495,"explanation":"Bipolar disorder includes episodes of elevated or unusually activated mood as well as depressive episodes. Mania is not merely happiness; it can disrupt judgment, sleep and social functioning.","paragraphIndex":20027,"bullets":[{"label":"Mania and hypomania","explanation":"Mania involves marked activation and impaired functioning; hypomania is a milder elevation that helps distinguish bipolar subtypes.","paragraphIndex":20028},{"label":"Course","explanation":"Episodes can recur and often emerge in adolescence or early adulthood, with inherited vulnerability making an important contribution.","paragraphIndex":20029},{"label":"Mania","explanation":"Marked activation can include little need for sleep, rapid speech, inflated confidence, distractibility, and risky actions.","paragraphIndex":78218},{"label":"Diagnostic differences","explanation":"Bipolar I involves full manic episodes; bipolar II includes hypomania together with major depression. A changeable ordinary mood is not enough to establish either diagnosis.","paragraphIndex":78219}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Bipolar disorder involves episodes of unusually elevated or irritable mood and activation, often alternating with depression. Mania and hypomania differ in severity and consequences.","followUpParagraphIndex":49409,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"standard_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h11","title":"Treatments","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m14-2-h10","printedPage":477,"pdfPage":495,"explanation":"Treatment of bipolar disorder aims to stabilize mood across time rather than simply remove current sadness or excitement. The biological mechanisms differ from those of standard depression treatment.","paragraphIndex":20030,"bullets":[{"label":"Lithium","explanation":"Lithium has a long history of effectiveness, but its useful and toxic levels can be close, making careful professional monitoring necessary.","paragraphIndex":20031},{"label":"Other supports","explanation":"Some anticonvulsant medicines and attention to regular sleep are important; choosing treatment requires the clinical course and medical context.","paragraphIndex":20032},{"label":"Lithium","explanation":"The textbook discusses lithium salts as a historically important and continuing treatment. Effects involve broader cellular mechanisms than a simple replacement for one deficient transmitter.","paragraphIndex":78220},{"label":"Need for careful follow-up","explanation":"Treatment options involve effectiveness, adverse effects, and monitoring considerations. These are clinical decisions, not procedures to carry out from a study note.","paragraphIndex":78221}],"status":"original_classroom_note_sample","basis":"provided_book_pdf_and_markdown","followUpExplanation":"Treatment of bipolar disorder differs from treating depression alone because interventions must address both elevated and depressed phases and reduce recurrence.","followUpParagraphIndex":49410,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"},{"headingId":"bp14-m14-2-h12","title":"In Closing: The Biology of Mood Swings","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":478,"pdfPage":496,"explanation":"The key lesson is that disorders of mood involve interacting neural and psychological processes. The degree of persistence, loss of functioning, and change in patterns of mood and activity matters.","followUpParagraphIndex":49411,"depth":"comprehensive_masters_with_expanded_explanations","studyDepth":"concise_existing"}],"classroomParagraphs":["Major depressive disorder involves sustained changes in mood, motivation, interest and daily functioning that go beyond ordinary sadness after a disappointment. The textbook considers biological vulnerability alongside stress and experience.","Disturbances may include loss of pleasure, sleep and appetite changes, low energy, reduced concentration and harmful thoughts.","Duration, breadth and functional impairment matter; no single symptom or neurotransmitter measurement is sufficient to diagnose a person.","Depression runs in families partly because inherited factors shape vulnerability, but the genetics are complex and overlap with other psychiatric conditions.","Many genetic variants contribute small effects rather than one dominant depression gene.","Inborn vulnerability may change how a person responds to stress; the same stressful event does not lead everyone to the same outcome.","Painful experiences and prolonged stress can contribute to depression through psychological and physiological pathways. The relationship is bidirectional, not a simple one-way cause.","Repeated stress can alter hormonal and neural regulation of mood and motivation.","Pain can worsen depressive symptoms and depression can intensify the experience of pain; observing co-occurrence alone cannot identify the only direction of causality.","Antidepressant medicines affect signaling systems involved in mood, but their clinical benefits are not explained fully by the immediate increase or decrease of one transmitter.","Common medications alter monoamine transmission, often involving serotonin or norepinephrine, through different mechanisms.","Biochemical actions begin quickly, whereas meaningful mood improvement often takes longer, indicating that downstream adaptation and plasticity contribute.","The standard drugs discussed include selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and other agents that affect transmitter availability. Each class has benefits, limitations and possible adverse effects.","Blocking transporters can prolong transmitter availability at synapses; different drugs target different transporters or receptors.","Side effects, interactions and uneven response make monitoring and individualized clinical prescribing essential.","Researchers have questioned the claim that depression is simply caused by insufficient serotonin. The textbook contrasts immediate drug action with slower changes in neural functioning.","A reuptake-blocking drug can alter synaptic conditions rapidly, while improvement commonly develops after repeated dosing.","Changes involving brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), receptor activity and synaptic adaptation may help explain delayed effects, though no single account covers all cases.","Trials generally find benefits from antidepressant medication for some patients, but improvement varies widely and placebo comparison requires careful interpretation.","A difference can be statistically significant yet modest for a particular person's symptoms.","Some patients do not respond to the first medication and require reassessment; it is incorrect to present any one drug as universally effective.","The textbook reviews renewed clinical research into psychedelic-assisted interventions and related rapidly acting approaches, while noting important methodological limits.","Participants often notice whether they received a perception-altering substance, making blinding and placebo comparison difficult.","Promising early findings are not permission for unsupervised use; benefits, safety and durability must be evaluated under appropriate clinical conditions.","Psychotherapy and other interventions can change brain activity as well as thought and behavior. This challenges the false idea that psychological treatment is somehow separate from biology.","Learning different interpretations and coping behaviors can produce measurable change in the neural systems that support mood.","The chapter discusses electroconvulsive therapy, brain stimulation and sleep-related approaches for selected cases; their mechanisms, benefits and drawbacks differ.","Bipolar disorder includes episodes of elevated or unusually activated mood as well as depressive episodes. Mania is not merely happiness; it can disrupt judgment, sleep and social functioning.","Mania involves marked activation and impaired functioning; hypomania is a milder elevation that helps distinguish bipolar subtypes.","Episodes can recur and often emerge in adolescence or early adulthood, with inherited vulnerability making an important contribution.","Treatment of bipolar disorder aims to stabilize mood across time rather than simply remove current sadness or excitement. The biological mechanisms differ from those of standard depression treatment.","Lithium has a long history of effectiveness, but its useful and toxic levels can be close, making careful professional monitoring necessary.","Some anticonvulsant medicines and attention to regular sleep are important; choosing treatment requires the clinical course and medical context.","The key lesson is that disorders of mood involve interacting neural and psychological processes. Neither a stressful event nor a measured transmitter level is a complete explanation.","Genes, stress responses, learning, sleep, plasticity and treatment effects all contribute to understanding mood episodes.","Compare major depression with bipolar disorder and explain why the time course of drug effects challenged early simple transmitter-deficit theories."],"classroomResearch":{"title":"Essential evidence: delayed antidepressant response","body":"Drugs that change monoamine signaling can affect synapses quickly, yet clinical benefit often emerges after repeated treatment.
